mbm-1926.clue: I keep one print inside its negative sleeve.
mbm-1926.quote: The picture is just my mother threading a needle by a window. In the negative the thread shows up black against her white hand. I like them together, like a day shift and a night shift.

mbm-1927.clue: I put the slowest fish in charge.
mbm-1927.quote: I wrote an aquarium screensaver. One fish got stuck at the edge, so I gave him a ticket booth. Now the other fish queue for bubbles while he sits in exactly the same spot.

mbm-1928.clue: I ask for the oldest thing in the room.
mbm-1928.quote: I thought the guide would point at a necklace. She pointed instead to a tiny fossil inside the stone plinth. I drew the plinth, fossil and all, and put the necklace in the corner.

mbm-1929.clue: I borrowed a towel for the plot.
mbm-1929.quote: I heard two neighbors arguing across their balconies. I couldn't hear a word over the traffic, only see a towel striped red, white and blue waving between them. I wrote both halves of the argument on the bench downstairs.

mbm-1930.clue: That navy stripe has been round the world.
mbm-1930.quote: My aunt sent me her old steward's apron when she finished sailing. I stitched the blue hem round a quilt of little boats. Her hem knows more ports than the boats ever will.

mbm-1931.clue: The bakery bell belongs to a pirate.
mbm-1931.quote: I write radio plays in my spare time. The bell over my neighbour's bakery door sounds exactly like a ship's bell. Each time someone buys bread I add a new ship to the harbor scene.

mbm-1932.clue: I press my thumb in the middle for the steam.
mbm-1932.quote: I showed my cousin how to open an arepa without burning his fingers. His first one split like a mouth. Now he draws little eyes with beans and makes his lunch greet everybody.

mbm-1933.clue: I found a second sun on the trail.
mbm-1933.quote: Something flashed under the lookout rock. It was a scrap of mirror left in the dirt. I picked it up in a spare sock and took it down with me. My friend says I've hiked home carrying the sun.

mbm-1934.clue: My family plays with an extra lamppost.
mbm-1934.quote: A candle dripped on our game board during a power cut. The wax was so neat Dad declared it a public lamppost and had me paint it yellow. Pieces on that square can always read the instructions.

mbm-1935.clue: I can tell you which train brings the carnations.
mbm-1935.quote: Every Friday a florist gets off the afternoon local carrying an armful of pink flowers. I got the train down in pencil before she arrived. I saved the next page for the carnations.

mbm-1936.clue: I swim the last lap with the clouds.
mbm-1936.quote: Our outdoor pool has one empty lane by the fence. On my back I can see a long stripe of sky between the flags. I save that view for the end, even on gray days.

mbm-1937.clue: I had to learn the wall by touch.
mbm-1937.quote: Fog settled over our pool so thick I could only see the blue tiles below me. I swam the slowest lap of my week. It felt like I was the first person to discover the other end.

mbm-1938.clue: I can hear my best find from the next room.
mbm-1938.quote: At a jumble sale I bought a clock that chimes the hour one note too high. The woman selling it hummed along when I tested it. She taught me the note before I took it home.

mbm-1939.clue: I stitched a ramp up to the red square.
mbm-1939.quote: I put my niece's toy railway into patchwork. Her station master's tiny wheelchair had no way onto my stitched platform, so she designed the ramp in a scrap of red ribbon herself.

mbm-1940.clue: I landed barefoot, according to the frog.
mbm-1940.quote: My boot printed every groove in the soft mud at the edge of the drop zone. By the time I got the camera a frog was sitting in the heel. I let him keep the landing record.

mbm-1941.clue: I followed the mark on the flood wall.
mbm-1941.quote: Our guide showed us a brass flood marker. I crouched to put my shoulder level with it. My aunt recognized her old street in a photograph above it. That evening we had tea with a woman who'd helped carry her upstairs.

mbm-1942.clue: I water-skied past a particularly sleepy dog.
mbm-1942.quote: Every summer morning the white spaniel on the houseboat sleeps through our first run. One day he stood up halfway along the dock and stretched. We all waved as if royalty had come to inspect us.

mbm-1943.clue: I call the yellow house pin the landlord.
mbm-1943.quote: One pin in our alley has a darker stripe than the others. It seems to survive every spare. The time I finally got it, the desk clerk rang the bell and announced I'd paid the rent.

mbm-1944.clue: The pencil marks on this mug are time zones.
mbm-1944.quote: I draw a little sun on my radio mug for every friend checking in from morning. On late nights there's sunrise all the way round my tea before it reaches me.

mbm-1945.clue: I like that flash of green in the gray.
mbm-1945.quote: I quilted a city street from old suit fabric. I stitched in two bright leaves for the weeds that came up between the stones under the doorstep at our first flat.

mbm-1946.clue: We let the fish choose the first player.
mbm-1946.quote: We keep our painted counters in a bowl and hold them up to the aquarium glass one by one. Whoever's color the goldfish noses at gets first turn. He's chosen red for a suspicious number of weeks.

mbm-1947.clue: My paper plaza fits behind an ear.
mbm-1947.quote: I folded a strip of tissue into little arches for my niece's dollhouse. I was going to make one strand. She handed me another color and said the square was having a festival.

mbm-1948.clue: The statue sees more than we do.
mbm-1948.quote: On a sightseeing trip I drew the square from behind its bronze mayor, trying to see his view. Nobody else had drawn the little bakery across the street. Its owner put my sketch in the window.

mbm-1949.clue: I buy the loose button at the bottom.
mbm-1949.quote: At the flea market there's a jar of splendid buttons. I always dig for the odd one that's rolled under the rest. I came home with an enamel plum blossom my aunt recognized from an old coat.

mbm-1950.clue: We save two seats for the thunder.
mbm-1950.quote: Our little cinema's roof booms in heavy rain. When the hero sailed into a storm, the whole audience looked up for the sound effect. The owner bowed to the ceiling.
